title: Take-Two Boss Unfazed by Bad Press for GTA 6 Launch
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick says he is not in the least concerned that bad press surrounding Rockstar's employment tribunal will affect GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Take-Two CEO Addresses Controversy Ahead of GTA 6

According to a recent report by Eurogamer, Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick has stated that he is "not in the least" concerned that the negative press surrounding Rockstar Games—specifically regarding alleged union-busting and employment tribunals—will have any impact on the highly anticipated launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.

## The Commercial Weight of GTA 6

In recent times, employment practices and workplace culture within the video game industry have faced intense scrutiny from media outlets, labor advocates, and players alike. Rockstar Games has not been immune to these discussions, with various reports and tribunal issues drawing public attention. Despite this, Take-Two's leadership remains entirely confident in the resilience of its biggest franchise.

As one of the most eagerly awaited entertainment products in history, GTA 6 commands unprecedented market attention. Zelnick's recent remarks suggest that the publisher believes the immense consumer demand and cultural footprint of the Grand Theft Auto series will remain unaffected by ongoing corporate or employment-related controversies.

## Editor's Take

It is hardly surprising that Take-Two's chief executive is brushing off external controversies given the astronomical commercial weight of GTA 6. Consumer demand for this franchise operates on a scale entirely of its own. However, the friction between corporate publishing giants and workplace advocacy highlights ongoing industry-wide challenges that continue to demand attention alongside blockbuster releases.
